facts.text: A stockpile is a pile of loose material waiting to be used; a dump point is where a truck tips its load; and a tip point or tip head is the active edge of a dump where trucks and a dozer work together.
facts.quote: A stockpile is a pile of loose material waiting to be used, a dump point is where a truck tips its load, and a tip point or tip head is the active edge of a dump where trucks and a dozer work together.

facts.text: Loading and dumping operations involve machines deliberately driving close to large objects and to each other.
facts.quote: All of this means machines deliberately driving close to large objects and to each other.

facts.text: Stockpiles, dump points and tip heads concentrate both deaths and nuisance alarms.
facts.quote: These places concentrate both deaths and nuisance alarms.

facts.text: Of 12 US dump-point deaths, six involved trucks reversing over the edge and six involved ground failures.
facts.quote: Of 12 US dump-point deaths, six were trucks reversing over the edge and six were ground failures [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Backing toward a rock pile for loading is a nuisance-detection scenario involving a real object, a slow intended approach and a driver who knows the object is there.
facts.quote: backing toward a rock pile for loading is the textbook nuisance detection: a real object, a slow intended approach, a driver who knows it is there [Chapter 4].

facts.text: South African guidance says a fixed stop distance could prevent machines being loaded from coming close enough, requiring the system to be switched off.
facts.quote: South African guidance says that with a fixed stop distance, machines being loaded could not come close enough and the system would have to be switched off [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Volvo's loader system remembers the last slope climbed to avoid braking when reversing down a stockpile.
facts.quote: Volvo's loader system remembers the last slope climbed precisely to avoid braking when reversing down a stockpile [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The collision mitigation system must distinguish an intended approach to a pile from an intrusion into the same space by a second truck or a person.
facts.quote: The system must tell an intended approach to a pile from an intrusion into the same space by a second truck or a person

facts.text: The collision mitigation system must not learn to ignore repeated berm alarms at a dump edge, because the object is genuinely dangerous.
facts.quote: must not "learn away" repeated berm alarms at a dump edge, where the object really is dangerous [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Loading and dumping must be treated as separate validation scenarios.
facts.quote: Loading and dumping are separate validation scenarios.
